//: The SECURITY FLOOR for framework pins, as reviewed data the `version-sync` gate judges the RESOLVED lockfile against. WHY THIS IS NOT osv-scan: the osv-scan PR lane is DIFF-AWARE and fails only on NEWLY introduced vulnerabilities, so a tree that has been shipping a vulnerable pin since before the advisory never reds on it — which is exactly the state this harness was in (it shipped `next: 16.2.7` for the two releases after 2026-07-20). The full-tree osv lane is schedule/push-only and network-and-clock dependent, so it cannot be a chain step. This file is the complement: CLOCKLESS, OFFLINE, DETERMINISTIC, and it reds in step 11 on every machine including a developer's with no network. osv-scan owns time-based DISCOVERY; this owns the floor a reviewer has already accepted. NOT A MIRROR OF OSV: one row per advisory a maintainer has read and decided about — a `packages` map that tried to mirror a vulnerability database would be stale the day it shipped and nobody would trust a red from it. `minPatchByMajor` is keyed by MAJOR LINE because that is the shape upstream security releases actually take (one patched release per supported line), and a single flat `minPatch` would wrongly red a consumer legitimately sitting on an older but PATCHED line. A major with NO entry is judged unsupported — derived, not a second hand-maintained `unsupportedMajors` list to drift against this one. OWNERSHIP: harness-OWNED, deliberately NOT seeded and deliberately NOT in ESCAPE_LISTS — `update` refreshes it (a new advisory must reach existing installs, which is the whole point) and `gate-integrity` sha-pins everything under tools/, so a consumer cannot lower a floor without redding step 2. `reviewedUntil` is judged in TWO halves, and the split is the point. WHETHER IT HAS LAPSED is a wall-clock question and rides the scheduled `floor-review` CI job, never the chain: a date-dependent verdict in `pnpm validate` would red an unchanged tree on a morning nobody chose, the exact non-determinism gates-catalog.md rules out. WHETHER THE WINDOW WAS LEGITIMATE is arithmetic over two committed dates, so it rides `version-sync` in the chain (0.6.0): reviewedUntil - reviewedOn must be <= 31 days, one calendar month, because upstream security releases now arrive on a roughly MONTHLY published cadence and a window longer than the cadence is one that can hide a whole release. This file shipped with a 92-day window — about three releases — and nothing anywhere objected, because the only control that read the date was the one an over-long date disarms. The reviewer now supplies WHEN THEY LOOKED; the harness supplies HOW LONG THAT IS WORTH. SOURCE: https://nextjs.org/blog/next-security-release-program

next.why: apps/web is the API host: it mounts the tRPC router, runs every Server Action, and its proxy.ts sits in front of both. All four HIGH advisories in the July 2026 release land on surfaces this scaffold ships by default. The two CRITICAL advisories in the August 2026 release are narrower AS SHIPPED — the scaffold is App Router only, configures no images.remotePatterns and targets a Linux deploy — but the /_next/image endpoint exists by default, consumers add remote images and self-host, and upstream patched no 16.2 release, so every install below the floor is on a line with a known unauthenticated RCE and no patch. The CRITICAL advisory the 2.0.0 review read, GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j, is narrower again AS SHIPPED — the scaffold imports nothing from next/og — but an Open Graph image route that passes request data into the Node.js ImageResponse is one import away for a consumer, and upstream patched no 16.2 release, so the 16.x floor moves to 16.3.6, the first fixed release. The 15.x line is outside its range and keeps 15.5.24. The five advisories the 2.0.1 review read (published upstream 2026-09-30, none in OSV on 2026-10-03) all name their fix as an unannounced 16.3 or 15.5 patch. Four land on no surface this scaffold ships AS SHIPPED: the SSRF needs images.remotePatterns, the two cache poisonings need the Pages Router or a root catch-all with SSG or ISR, and the metadata-image disclosure needs an image route under dynamicParams: false. The fifth, the MCP disclosure, reaches every install's next dev and no production build. Each of the four is a consumer's next feature away, so the floor moves to the newest releases on both lines, 16.3.8 and 15.5.27, published the day the advisories were, and each row records that the advisory has not yet said which release fixes it. The three advisories the 2026-10-17 review read (published upstream 2026-10-14, none in OSV that day) name their fixes, 16.4.1 and 15.5.28, and upstream patched no 16.3 release, so the 16.x floor crosses a minor. One lands on the scaffold AS SHIPPED: the Server Actions denial of service, because the web half is built on Server Actions. The Image Optimization RCE needs SVG input to the /_next/image endpoint, which exists by default, and the use cache RCE needs a use cache function returning typed arrays, which the scaffold has none of; upstream says to upgrade regardless. The floor moves to the fixed releases, 16.4.1 and 15.5.28. The seven advisories the 2026-11-08 review read (published upstream 2026-11-03, none in OSV that day) are Moderate and name their fixes: 16.4.5 for all seven, and 15.5.29 for the three that reach the 15 line. None lands on the scaffold AS SHIPPED: four need Cache Components or a use cache function, which the scaffold does not enable or have; the response injection needs a route handler that returns a fetched response unchanged, behind a pipelining HTTP/1.1 proxy; the cookie exposure needs an Edge route, and the scaffold's route handlers run on Node.js; and the SVG bypass needs an attacker-controlled image from a source the app allows, on a self-hosted /_next/image endpoint, which exists by default. Each is a consumer's next feature away, so the floor moves to the fixed releases, 16.4.5 and 15.5.29.

advisories.summary: Response injection and disclosure across clients in self-hosted applications that return a fetched upstream response unchanged from an App Router route handler (the advisory names the fetch cache too): the response's declared framing can disagree with the body sent, and behind an HTTP/1.1 reverse proxy that queues pipelined requests on a shared backend connection, a crafted upstream response can give one client another client's response. The scaffold's two route handlers return no fetched response; a consumer who adds one and self-hosts behind such a proxy is affected. Affects >= 16.0.0 <= 16.4.4 and <= 15.5.28, fixed in 16.4.5 and 15.5.29 (Moderate, CVSS v4 6.3). Published upstream 2026-11-03 (CVE-2026-119348).

Cross-user cache disclosure and poisoning when binary arguments (Uint8Array or Blob values) are passed to a use cache function: distinct arguments can produce one cache key, so a caller can receive another user's cached result or have theirs served to others. The scaffold has no use cache function. Affects >= 16.0.0 <= 16.4.4, fixed in 16.4.5; the 15.x line is outside the range (Moderate, CVSS v4 6.3). Published upstream 2026-11-03 (CVE-2026-119349).

Cache poisoning of a shared fallback shell in self-hosted applications served with next start and built with cacheComponents: true and partialPrefetching unset or false: on a route of the shape the advisory describes, one unauthenticated GET stores a persistent 404, or the attacker's value for a param in the server-rendered HTML, for every URL that shares the shell. The scaffold does not enable cacheComponents; upstream's workaround is partialPrefetching: true. Affects >= 16.4.0 <= 16.4.4, fixed in 16.4.5; the 15.x line is outside the range (Moderate, CVSS v4 6.3). Published upstream 2026-11-03 (CVE-2026-119350).

SVG rejection bypass in Image Optimization on self-hosted deployments: /_next/image can be made to process an attacker-supplied SVG even with dangerouslyAllowSVG: false (the default), reaching an SVG parser the application meant to keep off and exposing it to denial of service and decoder flaws. Upstream's release post adds that the image must come from a source the application allows. The /_next/image endpoint exists in every install by default, and the scaffold configures no images.remotePatterns. Affects >= 16.0.0 <= 16.4.4 and >= 15.0.0 <= 15.5.28, fixed in 16.4.5 and 15.5.29 (Moderate, CVSS v4 6.9). Published upstream 2026-11-03 (CVE-2026-119347).

Disclosure across root params when one use cache function that reads a root param is called both directly and through unstable_cache(): in the first fill after a process start, a deduplication race can store the result for one root param value (a locale or a tenant) under a key without root params, served for every value until it is revalidated or evicted. The scaffold has no use cache function and no unstable_cache() call; not calling a use cache function through unstable_cache(), which is unsupported, is a complete workaround. Affects >= 16.3.0 <= 16.4.4, fixed in 16.4.5; the 15.x line is outside the range (Moderate, CVSS v4 6.3; upstream's release post calls it High). Published upstream 2026-11-03 (CVE-2026-119790).

Cache leak across root param values in nested use cache functions with Cache Components enabled: when the inner function reads a root param and returns a value that still holds pending promises, the outer entry can be stored under a key without that root param and served for every value. Which value leaks is not attacker-chosen. A variant of GHSA-h694-7cp9-m8p3 that its fix does not cover. The scaffold enables no Cache Components and has no use cache function. Affects >= 16.2.0 <= 16.4.4, fixed in 16.4.5; the 15.x line is outside the range (Moderate, CVSS v4 6.3). Published upstream 2026-11-03 (CVE-2026-119351).

HttpOnly cookie exposure on Edge runtime routes: an App Router route handler or a Pages Router API route on the Edge runtime that sets a cookie through NextResponse also sends it in the internal x-middleware-set-cookie response header, which same-origin JavaScript can read. Exploiting it needs attacker-controlled script on the same origin. The scaffold has no Edge route: both its route handlers declare the Node.js runtime. Affects >= 16.0.0 <= 16.4.4 and >= 15.0.0 <= 15.5.28, fixed in 16.4.5 and 15.5.29 (Moderate, CVSS v4 6.0). Published upstream 2026-11-03 (CVE-2026-119346).

Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in the Image Optimization API when SVG files are used, through a memory-safety flaw in an upstream image library, on glibc-based Linux. The /_next/image endpoint exists in every install by default, and the scaffold's deploy target is Linux. Affects >= 10.0.0 <= 15.5.27 and > 16.0.0 <= 16.4.0, fixed in 15.5.28 and 16.4.1; upstream's workaround is sharp >= 0.35.5, which the fixed releases require. Published upstream 2026-10-14 (CVE-2026-96889).

Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in App Router applications using Cache Components, when a use cache function returns multiple typed arrays. The scaffold has no use cache function; a consumer who adds one is affected, and upstream knows no workaround and says to upgrade regardless. Affects >= 16.0.0 <= 16.4.0, fixed in 16.4.1; the 15.x line is outside the range. Published upstream 2026-10-14, no CVE id assigned on the day of review.

Denial of Service in App Router applications with at least one Server Action: crafted requests cause excessive CPU usage that blocks further requests in the same process. The scaffold's web half is built on Server Actions, so this reaches it as shipped; no workaround exists. Affects >= 13.0.0 <= 15.5.27 and >= 16.0.0 <= 16.4.0, fixed in 15.5.28 and 16.4.1. Published upstream 2026-10-14, no CVE id assigned on the day of review.

Server-side request forgery in Image Optimization: an allow-listed remote image URL can be used to make the server request private IP addresses. Only applications that configure images.remotePatterns are affected; the scaffold configures none, and a consumer who adds remote images is. Affects >= 16.0.0 < 16.3.? (CVSS 8.3). Published upstream 2026-09-30 (CVE-2026-94483). Upstream lists the patched version as an unannounced patch ("16.3.?") on 2026-10-03, so no release is confirmed fixed; the floor moves to 16.3.8, the newest release on the line, published the same day as the advisory.

Cache poisoning of SSG and ISR pages in self-hosted applications on the Pages Router: a page's cache entry can be replaced with another route's content, served to every visitor until revalidation. The scaffold is App Router only and has no SSG or ISR page; a consumer who adds Pages Router static pages and self-hosts is affected. Affects >= 15.0.0 and >= 16.0.0 (CVSS 6.3, Moderate). Published upstream 2026-09-30 (CVE-2026-94543). Upstream lists the patched version as an unannounced patch ("15.5.?, 16.3.?") on 2026-10-03, so no release is confirmed fixed; the floor moves to 15.5.27 and 16.3.8, the newest release on the line, published the same day as the advisory.

Cache poisoning in SSG and ISR rendering through a root-level catch-all page: a crafted request can corrupt the shared response cache, serving poisoned content to later users and denying service. The scaffold has no catch-all route and no SSG or ISR; a consumer who adds both is affected. Affects >= 15.0.0 and >= 16.0.0 (CVSS 6.3, Moderate). Published upstream 2026-09-30 (CVE-2026-94484). Upstream lists the patched version as an unannounced patch ("15.5.?, 16.3.?") on 2026-10-03, so no release is confirmed fixed; the floor moves to 15.5.27 and 16.3.8, the newest release on the line, published the same day as the advisory.

Information disclosure in App Router metadata image routes built with webpack: they ignore dynamicParams, so a dynamic segment excluded from generateStaticParams() can still be rendered on request. The scaffold has no metadata image route; a consumer who adds one under dynamicParams: false is affected. Affects >= 16.0.0 (CVSS 6.3, Moderate). Published upstream 2026-09-30 (CVE-2026-94485). Upstream lists the patched version as an unannounced patch ("16.3.?") on 2026-10-03, so no release is confirmed fixed; the floor moves to 16.3.8, the newest release on the line, published the same day as the advisory.

Information disclosure through the development server's Model Context Protocol endpoint, which checks no origin, so a malicious website open in the developer's browser can read project information. next dev only; production builds and deployments are not affected, and every install that runs next dev is. Affects >= 16.0.0. Published upstream 2026-09-30 (CVE-2026-94486). Upstream lists the patched version as an unannounced patch ("16.3.?") on 2026-10-03, so no release is confirmed fixed; the floor moves to 16.3.8, the newest release on the line, published the same day as the advisory.

Remote Code Execution in the Node.js ImageResponse of next/og when an application passes attacker-controlled values into SVG content, attributes or styles during image generation, through an upstream vulnerability in satori (GHSA-wx4j-mvgx-mqwp). The Edge ImageResponse is not affected. Affects >= 16.2.0 < 16.3.6, fixed in 16.3.6; the 15.x line is outside the range. Published upstream 2026-09-22 (CVE-2026-94545). The row carries the GHSA id because OSV lists the CVE as related, not as an alias, so a row keyed on the CVE would not match OSV's record of it.

Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in the Image Optimization API when Next.js optimizes an attacker-controlled AVIF image, via the libheif library under sharp (upstream GHSA-g89c-p67h-r497). The patched releases disable AVIF optimization until an upstream fix propagates. No CVE id was assigned on the day of review.

Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in applications using both the Pages Router and App Router without Cache Components when the server uses a Windows filesystem (GHSA-p293-qw3h-jr36). Linux and macOS are not affected; no known workaround on Windows.
Denial of Service in App Router using Server Actions — crafted requests cause excessive CPU usage that blocks further requests in the same process.
Middleware/proxy bypass in App Router apps built with Turbopack and a single config.i18n.locales entry — any auth or security check the middleware performs is bypassed.
SSRF via rewrites()/redirects() whose external destination hostname is built from request-controlled input; Open Redirect for the redirects case.
SSRF in Server Actions on custom servers — a forwarded or redirected request can be aimed at a malicious host when the attacker controls Host-associated headers.
Unauthenticated disclosure of internal Server Function endpoint ids (reconnaissance).
Denial of Service in the Image Optimization API via malicious remotely-hosted SVGs (self-hosted, default loader, remote images configured).
Unbounded Server Action payload in the Edge runtime leads to memory consumption.
Cache confusion of response bodies for fetch requests whose bodies contain invalid UTF-8 byte sequences.
Cache confusion of response bodies for `fetch(new Request(init), aDifferentInit)` calls carrying request bodies.
